Subject: Initial ask — hosted per-1M IO baseline + model roster

Hi Marissa,

We're evaluating hosted inference vendors and I wanted to get a quick baseline from Redwood on per-1M token pricing (we split input vs output). Would you be able to share the standard IO rates for hosted API across your most commonly used models, and a short model roster (small/medium/large variants) you recommend for a product like ours (real-time chat + embeddings for search)?

Also curious about:
- Starter discount for pilots (1–3 months, <2M tokens/mo)
- Indicative committed discount tiers (100k / 1M / 10M tokens/mo)
- Any restrictions on model variants for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments

We currently estimate ~3M tokens/mo for the first 3 months, ramping to ~20M by Q4. I can attach a quick volume estimate if that helps. Procurement is cc'd.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min sync if it's easier.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Product, Orion AI
elena@orionai.com

Subject: Re: Initial ask — hosted per-1M IO baseline + model roster

Hi Elena — great to meet you over email and thanks for the context.

Short answer up front: yes — we can provide a baseline IO rate and a recommended model roster for your workload, and we offer committed discount schedules for predictable usage. Attached is our standard hosted ratecard for Q3 for quick reference (pdf). Below are the baseline per-1M token rates (USD) for hosted API — list is input / output: 

- redwood-7b-instruct: $0.60 / $1.20 per 1M tokens
- redwood-13b-instruct: $1.20 / $2.40 per 1M tokens
- redwood-33b: $2.10 / $4.20 per 1M tokens
- open-quant-6b (quantized): $0.42 / $0.84 per 1M tokens
- embeddings-large (prod embed model): $3.50 per 1M embedding units (single-sided)

Notes:
- Input tokens are billed at the input rate; output tokens at the output rate. Embeddings are billed per embedding unit.
- Rates above are list (no commit). We commonly recommend redwood-7b-instruct for latency-sensitive chat and redwood-13b-instruct for higher-quality responses when latency budgets allow.

For committed discounts, we typically propose:
- 10% off list for a 6-month 1M tokens/mo commit
- 20% off list for a 12-month 5M tokens/mo commit
- 30% off list for a 12-month 15M tokens/mo commit
(Exact tiers are negotiable and dependent on seat/license add-ons and ingress/egress needs.)

If you can send the quick volume estimate (monthly ramp) I'll run a tailored commit schedule and put together a short MSD (mutual action plan) + pricing term sheet.

Attachments: redwood_hosted_ratecard_q3.pdf (rate matrix + model availability notes)

Next step: would you like a 20-min call tomorrow to walk the roster and discounts?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for LLMs

Hi Elena / Procurement team — thanks for the volume sheet. Below is a concise response and proposed next steps.

1) Latency (us-west, hosted API, 128-token output, baseline network):
- redwood-7b-instruct: p95 ~ 220ms
- redwood-13b-instruct: p95 ~ 420ms
- redwood-33b: p95 ~ 980ms (note: may vary with batching and concurrent load)
(These are typical production figures for our hosted fleet; we can share tracing on a short demo call.)

2) Committed discounts (applies as % off list; we can optionally price larger models separately for very large commitments):
- Pilot offer: 15% off list for first 2 months up to 3M tokens/mo
- Tier A: 10% off list for 6-month 1M tokens/mo commit
- Tier B: 20% off list for 12-month 5M tokens/mo commit
- Tier C: 30% off list for 12-month 15M tokens/mo commit

Note: For commitments that include heavy usage of redwood-33b we typically handle pricing on a case-by-case basis (usually within the Tier B/C framework but with a model-specific uplift).

3) Quantized models (open-quant-6b): good for cost-sensitive, high-throughput scenarios — we recommend A/B testing on your chat flows. Quality delta is task-dependent; for conversational chat the regressions are minimal in many contexts but for tight factual summarization you may prefer redwood-13b.

4) Seat/minimums: no mandatory seat fees for hosted commits; we have optional support tiers and premium observability add-ons that are licensed separately.

Attachments included: redwood_committed_discount_template.pdf (sample term sheet + MAD template). I'll also create a short HubSpot deal (link below) so procurement can reference line items. If you're ready, next steps I propose:
- 20-min technical call with Ben to validate latency/quality and walk the Pilot config (we can run a 2-week demo with tracing)
- Procurement review MSA draft (I'll send an initial MSA + SOW for review)
- If Pilot looks good, convert to a 12-month commit with Tier B pricing and a signed SOW
